title: Nagy et al. (2012) · MUA ligand exchange for 3, 5 and 10 nm cores

conflictPairs.context: UV–vis formulas attributed to Yu et al. reference 61; bibliography lists Yu as 60 and Martin as 61. Referenced paper not reviewed.

Negative MUA/MPA: 20, 80, 160 µg/mL. Positive dose labels differ by assay/panel: general methods 0.5, 5, 20 µg/mL; Figures 2B, 3D, 4B, 5B use 0.5, 3.5, 20; Figure 3B images and Figures 5D/6 use their explicit labels. Never merge 3.5 and 5.
p.12 assigns mass/molar/particle conversion to SI Table 3; p.13 SI availability assigns it to SI Table 2. Neither table was inspected.
LDH method cites Martin et al.62; bibliography lists Martin as 61 and Gao as 62. Prior procedure not inspected.
General AUT toxicity wording is not interpreted as necrosis at every size/dose; specific low-dose exceptions retained.
Ethidium bromide (AO/EB heading, figure captions) versus ethidium iodide (p.13 method sentence) unresolved.
Results prose describes MUA apoptosis only 10 nm/160 µg/mL, while Table 4 summarizes positive counts for all three MUA sizes. Do not collapse table and prose into one claim.
Figure 4 exposure 22 h versus methods 24 h.
Figure 4B axis says absorbance while caption describes fold change; no curve numbers reinterpreted.
p.4 says MPA and CYST did not induce significant redox stress; p.10 and Table 4 report 5 nm MPA ROS increase, and Table 4 also marks one positive CYST 3 nm condition.
Figure 5B positive middle dose 3.5 µg/mL; Figure 5D explicitly 5 µg/mL.
Caption H2DCFDA versus method CM-H2DCFDA/full chemical name retained without identity correction.
Figure 6 headline says 3 nm MUA/AUT, but panels/legends and descriptions include 3,5,10 nm. Caption scope conflict retained.
Gene-selection wording differs: up/down ≥2-fold in discussion versus increased >2-fold in methods.
Discussion groups results across 20 and 0.5 µg/mL; tables retain their exact dose scope.
Discussion says CYP1A1/CYP1B1 over 40-fold for CYST; Table 3 CYP1A1 is 38.28 ±4.75, CYP1B1 47.60 ±0.32. Exact cells retained.
Table 4 positive/negative symbols are literal dose-count summaries, not effect sizes and not a replacement for conflicting prose or figure-specific dose labels.
p.2 says only 10 nm MUA fails the magnitude >30 mV stability threshold, but Table 1 also reports 5 nm MPA at −29.4 mV. Keep literal table values and prose distinct.

intuition.title: Source interpretation and limits
intuition.summary: Authors tentatively rank surface charge, functionalization/ligand length and core size in their NHBE cytotoxicity study; positive QDs generally cause stronger responses. Cd/Se balance and AUT interaction, mitochondrial injury/uncoupling, and ROS-independent toxicity are proposed explanations, not independently measured composition, uptake or a proven unique mechanism. Smaller/long-ligand and concentration effects retain assay-specific exceptions.

general_background.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
general_background.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
